result.summary: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-018.md in full and every changed file (eventStaff.ts, eventStaffAuthorization.ts, handlers/staff.ts, handlers/checkin.ts, user.ts's getUserByTgUsername, i18n additions, index.ts wiring) -- implementation matches the design's exact signatures/sequencing with no undocumented deviation. Independently re-derived all 6 ACs myself against real Postgres (fresh docker-compose.yml stack, drizzle-kit migrate) and a real grammy.Bot dispatching synthetic Update objects through bot.handleUpdate() with api.config.use() intercepting outbound sendMessage -- did not trust BACKEND-DEV's report. Seeded chapter, organizer (tgId 9001), target/volunteer (tgId 9002, tgUsername staffuser_req018), and a second owner-role user (tgId 9003), plus events A (future, staffed on this event only), B (future, never staffed), C (already-ended endsAt, staffed). AC1: staffed on A only, /checkin B refused with the generic 'not authorized to check people in' string; /checkin A (sanity control) authorized -- confirms event-specificity. AC2: same staff-only user's /venue_new (with a well-formed body, so the check under test is authorization, not the usage-arg short-circuit) and /event_publish both refused with the existing organizer-only string, role stayed 'member' throughout (confirmed by a direct SELECT) -- the 'registration list' third surface still does not exist anywhere in this codebase (git grep confirms), matching the design's own §6.5/AC2 note and the MINOR gap already flagged at step-01b; not re-litigated, no new information found. AC3: staffed on C (endsAt in the past relative to the real clock), /checkin C refused with the same generic string despite genuine staffing. AC4: captured the exact outbound payloads verbatim for both /staff_add and /staff_remove -- assignment body names the event ('Event B (not staffed, future)') and states the door role/procedure; removal body names the event and states access has ended; both delivered via a distinct sendMessage to the target's own chat id, language resolved via the target's own resolveLangForTg, not the organizer's. AC5: audit_log count for 'event_staff.add' 0->1 across exactly one /staff_add call, and 'event_staff.remove' 0->1 across exactly one /staff_remove call, counted before/after myself. AC6: my own git grep -n -i speaker -- apps/bot/src returned no matches (exit 1). Independently confirmed removeEventStaff's hard-DELETE-with-audit-write is a single db.transaction, byte-for-byte the same shape as venue.ts's deleteVenue (delete first, then one writeAuditLog call, same transaction) -- read both functions side by side. Independently confirmed the hard-delete: a direct SELECT on event_staff for (eventB, target) returned 0 rows after removal, and the very next /checkin B call from the same user was refused immediately with no cached permission. Critically re-checked checkEventStaffAuthorization's 'no role short-circuit' claim by reading the function body directly (not the domain test file's own assertions): its 4 steps are user===null, staffRow===null, isFinished(endsAt, evaluationTime), else ok -- role is never referenced anywhere in the function. Then verified this live and structurally: dispatched /checkin B from the organizer (role=organizer, no event_staff row for B) and from a freshly-seeded owner (role=owner, no event_staff row for B) -- both refused with the identical generic string, exactly like the plain-member case. This is the core S2 property and it holds both by code reading and by live dispatch. Confirmed /checkin's stub does genuinely nothing beyond authorize-and-acknowledge: read handlers/checkin.ts end to end -- no qr_token parsing, no registrations read/write, no AuditLog write on any path (checked git diff for any registrations/qr_token references in this diff: none). Confirmed no domain logic lives in either handler body -- staff.ts and checkin.ts only sequence calls into domain/eventAuthorization.ts, domain/event.ts, domain/eventStaff.ts, domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts, domain/user.ts and compose reply strings; every authorization/business rule lives in the framework-free domain modules (decisions/0004 compliance). Confirmed no now()/current_timestamp appears in any time-dependent predicate in the diff (git grep across the four new/touched domain+handler files: no matches) -- evaluationTime is threaded as an explicit new Date() parameter from the handler through requireEventStaffForEvent to checkEventStaffAuthorization, matching decisions/0006. Scope check: git diff master...HEAD --name-only touches only apps/bot/src/** plus docs/agents/design/REQ-018.md and this run's own handoffs/ bookkeeping -- no apps/web files, no unrelated changes. No schema change in this diff (confirmed against db/schema.ts: event_staff/audit_log tables are untouched, matching design section 1's own reasoning) -- no migration to review, so the S13 sign-off duty is not triggered here. Ran npm run lint (0 errors, the 2 pre-existing apps/web warnings are unrelated to this diff), npm run build (both workspaces, tsc clean), and npx vitest run independently: 10 files / 114 tests passed, matching BACKEND-DEV's reported count exactly. Design-system check: N/A, no visual/CSS surface in this bot-only change (matches design section 8's own reasoning, consistent with REQ-016/017 precedent). No anti-pattern from docs/agents/anti-patterns.md applies to this diff. Scratch verification script and docker-compose stack torn down after use (docker compose down -v); git status confirmed clean, no stray files.
result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) -- this is a bot requirement establishing security invariant S2 (EventStaff authorization is existence+expiry only, no role short-circuit), so the security gate is mandatory and especially important here.
